name: North American / Ryan Navion
manufacturer: North American Aviation / Ryan Aeronautical / Navion
summary: Rugged postwar four-seat retractable single designed by the makers of the P-51, with a sliding canopy and a tall stance.

wings: Low, moderately tapered wing with dihedral; wingtip tanks on some
engines: Single flat-six in a large cowl
fuselage: Sliding canopy over a deep, roomy cabin (Rangemaster has doors instead)
tail: Broad fin with straight leading edge and large horizontal tail

tellTales: Low-wing single with a sliding canopy and a tall stance on the ground
Thick wing and deep, robust fuselage with a fighter-like look

confusedWith.howToTell: The AA-5 is smaller with fixed gear and skinny tubular legs; the Navion is bigger with tall retractable gear.
The Bonanza has doors and a sleeker, longer fuselage; the Navion has a sliding canopy and a taller, chunkier stance.
The Comanche has a door, a stabilator and a slimmer fuselage; the Navion has a sliding canopy.
The Navion is a four-seater with a long canopy and tricycle gear; the Swift is a smaller two-seater with a tailwheel.
The Navion has a single fin, a nosewheel and a long canopy; the Cruisair has a triple-fin tail and a tailwheel.
